subject: biology
title: Photosynthesis & Respiration Basics
welcome_lead: Today you'll meet the two equations that power all life — photosynthesis and respiration.
meta_desc: GCSE Biology Bioenergetics foundations — photosynthesis, aerobic and anaerobic respiration equations.
final_note: You can now write the photosynthesis equation, both respiration equations, and say where each happens in the cell.

Plant cell part where photosynthesis happens
Releases energy using oxygen, in mitochondria
Releases energy without oxygen, less energy

walkthroughs.body_html:
Photosynthesis happens in chloroplasts inside plant leaves.

The word equation is:

carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen

It needs light energy (absorbed by chlorophyll) and the chemical reaction is endothermic — it takes in energy.

Plants use the glucose to grow, to make starch, and to release energy through respiration.

Aerobic respiration happens in mitochondria in every living cell — plant and animal.

The word equation is:

glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water (+ energy)

It's exothermic — it releases energy your body uses to move, grow, build new molecules, and stay warm.

When oxygen runs low (e.g. during a sprint), cells switch to anaerobic respiration.

In animal muscle: glucose → lactic acid

In yeast and plants (fermentation): glucose → ethanol + carbon dioxide

Anaerobic releases much less energy per glucose than aerobic — but it's fast. Fermentation is used to make bread (CO₂ rises the dough) and beer/wine (ethanol).

mcqs.q: Where in the cell does aerobic respiration happen?
options: Chloroplast
Nucleus
Mitochondrion
Ribosome

mcqs.q: What does yeast produce by anaerobic respiration?
options: Lactic acid only
Ethanol + carbon dioxide
Glucose + oxygen
Water + oxygen
Anaerobic respiration produces oxygen as a waste product.
Plants only photosynthesise and do not respire; respiration is for animals only.
Yes — plants respire all the time to release energy; they also photosynthesise when there is light.
Plants only respire at night and only photosynthesise during the day; the processes never overlap.

mcqs.q: Where do plants get most of their biomass from?
options: Plants gain most of their mass directly from sunlight, which has weight.
Plants get most of their mass from the soil through their roots.
From carbon dioxide in the air — the carbon in plant tissue comes mostly from CO2 fixed during photosynthesis.
Plants only respire at night and only photosynthesise during the day; the processes never overlap.

mcqs.q: What is produced in anaerobic respiration in human muscle cells?
options: Plants only respire at night and only photosynthesise during the day; the processes never overlap.
Anaerobic respiration produces oxygen as a waste product.
Lactic acid (lactate) and a small amount of ATP — no CO2 or water in this pathway.
Anaerobic respiration produces ethanol and CO2 in humans.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Lactic acid”?
options: Animal anaerobic product, builds up in muscles
Yeast anaerobic: makes ethanol + CO₂
Releases energy without oxygen, less energy
Plant cell part where photosynthesis happens

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Anaerobic respiration”?
options: Yeast anaerobic: makes ethanol + CO₂
Plant cell part where photosynthesis happens
Plants make glucose from CO₂ + water using light
Releases energy without oxygen, less energy

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Chloroplast”?
options: Plant cell part where photosynthesis happens
Plants make glucose from CO₂ + water using light
Releases energy using oxygen, in mitochondria
Yeast anaerobic: makes ethanol + CO₂

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Aerobic respiration”?
options: Plants make glucose from CO₂ + water using light
Yeast anaerobic: makes ethanol + CO₂
Releases energy using oxygen, in mitochondria
Animal anaerobic product, builds up in muscles

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Photosynthesis”?
options: Releases energy without oxygen, less energy
Plant cell part where photosynthesis happens
Plants make glucose from CO₂ + water using light
Releases energy using oxygen, in mitochondria

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Fermentation”?
options: Plant cell part where photosynthesis happens
Releases energy using oxygen, in mitochondria
Releases energy without oxygen, less energy
Yeast anaerobic: makes ethanol + CO₂

mcqs.q: A leaf cell respires 30 glucose molecules aerobically. Each glucose needs 6 oxygen molecules. How many oxygen molecules are used in total?
A student measures bubbles of gas from pondweed at different distances from a lamp. As the lamp moves closer, more bubbles form per minute. Which conclusion is supported?
options: Light intensity increases the rate of photosynthesis.
Temperature is limiting the rate of photosynthesis.
The pondweed is respiring faster as it gets darker.
Carbon dioxide is the gas being given off in respiration.

mcqs.q: A sealed test tube contains pondweed and an indicator that shows CO₂ level. After several hours in bright light the CO₂ level falls. Which best explains this?
options: Photosynthesis used up more CO₂ than respiration released.
The plant stopped respiring in the light.
Respiration released CO₂ faster than photosynthesis used it.
No gas exchange happened in the light.

mcqs.q: During a sprint, an athlete's muscles run short of oxygen. Which product would you expect to build up in the muscle cells?
options: Lactic acid
Ethanol
Glucose
Oxygen

mcqs.q: A student compares energy released from equal amounts of glucose by aerobic and anaerobic respiration. Which result is expected?
options: Aerobic respiration releases much more energy per glucose.
Anaerobic respiration releases more energy per glucose.
Both release exactly the same amount of energy.
Neither releases any energy from glucose.

numericals.q: A leaf cell respires 30 glucose molecules aerobically. Each glucose needs 6 oxygen molecules. How many oxygen molecules are used in total?

free_texts.q: What product builds up in your muscles when you respire anaerobically during exercise? Two words.

sequence.def: Glucose split into 2 pyruvate in cytoplasm; net 2 ATP
Pyruvate -> acetyl-CoA in matrix; CO2 released
Acetyl-CoA oxidised; makes NADH, FADH2 and CO2
NADH/FADH2 donate electrons along inner membrane
ATP synthase makes most ATP; O2 is final acceptor
